one_liner: SSE2/SSE4.1 global and extension DNA alignment (minimap2's kernel) using Suzuki-Kasahara 8-bit difference DP; beats parasail's 32-bit striped global aligners.
what_it_does: C library for affine and two-piece-affine gap DNA alignment of one pair of sequences: global, or extension with Z-drop, optionally banded, optionally with a CIGAR whose gaps are left- or right-aligned. There is no local alignment. Each ksw2_*.c file is one self-contained function (ksw_extz2_sse, ksw_extd2_sse, ksw_gg and so on) taking 0..m-1 encoded sequences, an int8 m*m score matrix, gap penalties, a band width, a Z-drop and flags, and filling a ksw_extz_t. It is not a drop-in for parasail, which takes character strings and a parasail matrix.
how_it_is_fast: Suzuki and Kasahara's difference recurrence stores the differences between neighbouring DP cells instead of absolute scores. The differences are bounded by the match and gap scores, so they fit in int8 lanes and one 128-bit register holds 16 cells whatever the total alignment score; parasail needs 32-bit lanes (4 per register) on 50 kb inputs. Cells are processed along anti-diagonals so the lanes in a vector have no dependency on each other, and SSE4.1 blendv/max replace the SSE2 emulation. Global score-only mode (-g, approximate max) stays 16-way through the whole inner loop; tracking the exact maximum for extension needs a 32-bit H array updated 4-way, which is why -s rows are about 3x slower than -sg.
when_to_use: Long DNA or nucleotide pairs (kilobases to tens of kilobases) with simple match/mismatch scoring where you need a global score or a Z-drop extension, e.g. read-to-reference extension as in minimap2
Score-only global alignment of long pairs on x86 SSE4.1: the README's 50 kb pair runs in 0.84 s against 2.2 s for parasail's best SSE4 row
Banded alignment with CIGAR (left- or right-aligned gaps) when you can bound the band width, which keeps traceback memory proportional to sequence length times band
Two-piece affine gaps (ksw_extd2_sse) to keep long indels from being split, or splice-aware alignment (ksw_exts2_sse)
Projects that want to vendor two files (ksw2.h plus one ksw2_*.c, MIT) with no dependencies
when_not_to_use: Local (Smith-Waterman) alignment or protein alignment with a full substitution matrix: no local mode, and the SSE kernels assume one match and one mismatch score (KSW_EZ_GENERIC_SC exists but the README says diagonal vectorisation is harder with generic matrices); use parasail or SSW

Traceback on long unbanded pairs: the direction matrix takes about (qlen+tlen) x min(qlen,tlen) bytes, so a 50 kb pair with CIGAR needs gigabytes; in issue #3 that run segfaulted from an integer overflow and the maintainer declined to fix it ('not worth increasing the peak memory')
Highly similar long sequences, where edit-distance or wavefront methods with dynamic banding (edlib, WFA2-lib) do far less work; the README itself points to edlib's dynamic banding
Targets without x86 SSE2: there are no AVX2, AVX-512 or NEON kernels here (avx2=1 only adds -mavx2), and only ksw2_extd2_sse.c has a USE_SIMDE switch

Code that needs a maintained upstream: this repository has had no commits since 2023-06-27, and correctness issues are open (#28 banded extd2_sse reports a score above the unbanded optimum, 1084 against 1078; #19 ksw_extd with tlen > qlen + w; #15 segfault in ksw_exts2_sse)

integration.dependencies: none (optional kalloc memory pool via HAVE_KALLOC; the ksw2-test CLI needs zlib; parasail and gaba only for the comparison build)
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler with SSE2 intrinsics (Makefile: gcc -O2 -march=native, -Wc++-compat so it also builds as C++); SSE4.1 optional at compile time, KSW_SSE2_ONLY forces SSE2
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 with SSE2 (SSE4.1 faster); KSW_CPU_DISPATCH hooks exist but the dispatcher file is not in this repo
integration.thread_safety: Functions keep no static or global state (none in ksw2_extz2_sse.c or ksw2_extd2_sse.c) and allocate from the caller's km pool, so separate threads with separate pools and ksw_extz_t structs are safe; kalloc's own thread safety is not documented

gotchas: ksw_extz2_sse returns without computing anything when -min_sc > 2*(q+e) (ksw2_extz2_sse.c line 82), i.e. when the mismatch penalty exceeds twice the gap-open-plus-extend cost, so ez keeps whatever it held before; initialise ez and keep mismatch penalties modest. Scores and penalties are int8 and mat[0] + 2*(q+e) must fit in an int8 lane.

When the wildcard (last) matrix entry is 0, as ksw_gen_simple_mat and the README example produce, the SSE kernel scores N as -e, not 0 (line 68 sets sc_N_ to -e), so ksw_extz2_sse and the scalar ksw_extz give different scores on sequences containing N (issue #11). Issue #25 (open) reports ez->mte_q set from en where en0 was meant.

The fastest README rows use -g (KSW_EZ_APPROX_MAX | KSW_EZ_APPROX_DROP): the global end score is built by summing exact cell differences along a path to the corner, and the code comment says only the tracked maximum and Z-drop become approximate, so extension callers that need the exact max must drop -g and pay about 3x (2.7 s against 0.84 s on the 50 kb pair).

Benchmark harness (cli.c): there is no internal timer, so the table is presumably whole-process wall time of one run, including gzip parsing, encoding and per-call calloc. parasail gets parasail_matrix_create("ACGTN", match, mismatch), which scores N against N as a match where ksw2 gives 0 (a TODO in the code); that does not matter for the N-free test pairs. parasail's nw_striped_32 is a dispatcher that would pick AVX2 on an AVX2 machine, and the CPU is not named.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ksw2 over parasail for long DNA with match/mismatch scoring when you need global or Z-drop extension alignment with a CIGAR; parasail wins on scoring generality, local and semi-global modes and wider SIMD. SSW covers local alignment with CIGAR, and WFA2-lib (which uses ksw2_extz2_sse as its baseline) is the better choice when the sequences are highly similar.
verified_claims_summary: README table, one run each, wall time in seconds. On the 50 kb phage pair (test/t2.fa.gz against test/q2.fa.gz, phage50k_ref and phage50k_mut90 per issue #3), global score only: ksw_extz2_sse with -sg takes 0.84 s (SSE4.1) and 0.96 s (SSE2), against 2.2 s for parasail nw_striped_32 (2.6x, derived from page data) and 7.3 s for ksw2's scalar Green DP (8.7x). On the 16.5 kb mitochondrial pair with CIGAR: 0.40 s against 1.6 s scalar, and 0.18 s with -g. CPU, compiler, parasail version and scoring parameters are not stated; the CLI defaults are match 2, mismatch -4, gap open 4, extend 2, and the Makefile builds with gcc -O2 -march=native.
status_note: Abandoned upstream since 2023-06-27 (last change: an int-overflow fix in gg2_sse allocation), with 2022 commits syncing it from minimap2, whose copy is the maintained one; MIT and two files to vendor, but check the open banded-score and segfault issues before relying on ksw_extd/ksw_exts2.
